provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Counting 11 and 12
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count 11 and 12
The pupils should be able to identify 11 and 12
Introduction:
We can count up to 10. Today we learn 11 and 12.
These numbers come after 10.
Content:
11 is ten and one more. 12 is ten and two more.
Use counters to show 11 and 12.
Trace the numbers with your fingers.
Class activity:
Give each pupil 12 counters. Count them together.
Evaluation questions:
What number comes after 10?
How many fingers do you have on one hand?
Show me 12 counters.
Summary:
Today we learned to count 11 and 12.

topics.title: Counting 13 and 14
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count 13 and 14
The pupils should be able to write 13 and 14
Introduction:
We learned 11 and 12 last week.
Today we learn 13 and 14.
Content:
13 is ten and three more. 14 is ten and four more.
Use stones to show 13 and 14.
Trace the numbers in the air.
Class activity:
Place 14 pebbles on the table. Remove one. Count again.
Evaluation questions:
What comes after 12?
How many legs does a chicken have?
Circle the number 14.
Summary:
We can now count 13 and 14.

topics.title: Counting 15 and 16
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count 15 and 16
The pupils should be able to match 15 and 16 objects
Introduction:
We can count up to 14 now.
Today we learn 15 and 16.
Content:
15 is ten and five more. 16 is ten and six more.
Use bottle caps to show 15 and 16.
Write the numbers on the board.
Class activity:
Give pupils 16 beans each. Group them in twos.
Evaluation questions:
What number comes after 14?
How many eggs are in one dozen?
Show me 15 fingers.
Summary:
Today we learned to count 15 and 16.

topics.title: Counting 17 and 18
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count 17 and 18
The pupils should be able to identify 17 and 18
Introduction:
We learned 15 and 16 last week.
Today we learn 17 and 18.
Content:
17 is ten and seven more. 18 is ten and eight more.
Use pencils to show 17 and 18.
Clap the numbers 17 and 18.
Class activity:
Place 18 pencils on the table. Take some away. Count what is left.
Evaluation questions:
What comes after 16?
How many sides does a stop sign have?
Write the number 18.
Summary:
We can now count 17 and 18.

topics.title: Counting 19 and 20
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count 19 and 20
The pupils should be able to trace 19 and 20
Introduction:
We can count up to 18 now.
Today we learn 19 and 20.
Content:
19 is ten and nine more. 20 is two tens.
Use erasers to show 19 and 20.
Trace the numbers with sandpaper.
Class activity:
Count 20 jumps together. Count 19 claps together.
Evaluation questions:
What comes after 18?
How many fingers do you have on both hands?
Show me 19 objects.
Summary:
Today we learned to count 19 and 20.

topics.title: Counting 1 to 20
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count from 1 to 20
The pupils should be able to fill missing numbers
Introduction:
We have learned all numbers up to 20.
Today we practice counting them all.
Content:
Count from 1 to 20 in order.
Say each number clearly.
Fill in missing numbers on a number line.
Class activity:
Stand in a circle. Each pupil says one number up to 20.
Evaluation questions:
Count from 1 to 20.
What number comes before 10?
Fill in the blank: 5, 6, __, 8.
Summary:
We can count from 1 to 20.

topics.title: Big and small
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify big objects
The pupils should be able to identify small objects
Introduction:
We have learned numbers up to 20.
Today we learn about size.
Content:
Big means large in size. Small means tiny in size.
Compare a big ball and a small ball.
Circle the big object on your worksheet.
Class activity:
Bring big and small toys from home. Sort them into two groups.
Evaluation questions:
Is a kerosene stove big or small?
Show me something small in the classroom.
Which is bigger, a danfo bus or a bicycle?
Summary:
We can now tell big things from small things.

topics.title: More and less
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify more objects
The pupils should be able to identify less objects
Introduction:
We learned about big and small last week.
Today we learn about more and less.
Content:
More means a bigger amount. Less means a smaller amount.
Compare two plates with different numbers of sweets.
Point to the plate with more sweets.
Class activity:
Give pupils two bags with different numbers of stones. Which has more?
Evaluation questions:
Which has more, 10 pencils or 5 pencils?
Show me a bag with less oranges.
If I have 5 naira and you have 3 naira, who has more?
Summary:
We can now tell which has more and which has less.

topics.title: Sorting and matching
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sort objects
The pupils should be able to match objects
Introduction:
We learned about more and less last week.
Today we learn sorting and matching.
Content:
Sorting means putting things in groups. Matching means pairing things.
Sort blocks by color. Match shoes in pairs.
Draw a line to match each object to its partner.
Class activity:
Give pupils different colored buttons. Sort them by color.
Evaluation questions:
How many buttons are red?
Match each shoe to its pair.
Sort these leaves by size.
Summary:
We can now sort and match objects.

topics.title: Revision
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count 1 to 20
The pupils should be able to identify big and small
The pupils should be able to find more and less
Introduction:
We have learned many things this term.
Today we practice all of them.
Content:
Count from 1 to 20. Play big or small game.
Play more or less game with sweets.
Review all topics from this term.
Class activity:
Count 20 jumps. Sort big and small leaves. Find which plate has more.
Evaluation questions:
Count from 1 to 20.
Show me something big in the classroom.
Which has less, 7 balls or 9 balls?
Match these socks.
Summary:
We have practiced all we learned this term.
